bull.b: The benchmark franchises are becoming an increasingly important earnings engine, combining strong growth with high incremental margins. Their scale, market relevance, and integration into financial products support durable recurring revenue and provide operating leverage as adoption expands.

Rapid growth in API usage and connected customers shows that S&P Global is embedding its data into emerging AI workflows. This can deepen client integration, support new consumption-based revenue, and strengthen the long-term value of its proprietary information assets.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and earnings quality
bull.b: Robust free cash flow closely tracking net income indicates that reported profitability is supported by substantial cash generation. This provides resources for product investment, acquisitions, debt management, and shareholder returns while reinforcing financial resilience over the coming quarters.

bear.b: Funding buybacks partly with new debt is expected to push leverage above management’s target range in 2026. Although natural deleveraging is expected by 2027, higher leverage temporarily reduces financial flexibility and increases sensitivity to weaker earnings or elevated financing costs.

S&P Global remains highly profitable, but the decline in trailing gross margin raises questions about near-term margin durability. If unfavorable mix or cost pressure persists, it could limit operating leverage and make the company’s otherwise strong earnings growth less consistent.

bear.t: Market Intelligence renewal and product softness
bear.b: Weakness in selected Market Intelligence products and slower renewals can delay subscription growth and reduce visibility in an important data business. Extended negotiations around AI, intellectual property, and token costs may also complicate monetization and prolong conversion of demand into revenue.
